claims.statement: Article 77 of the EU Batteries Regulation requires an electronic battery passport from 18 February 2027 for every LMT battery, industrial battery above 2 kWh, and EV battery placed on the market or put into service.

The regulation requires interoperability, free access according to access rights, restricted update rights, data integrity, security, and continued availability even if the responsible economic operator ceases activity.

A March 2026 European Parliament question identifies outstanding standards, registry, service-provider, and access-rule work and explicitly questions whether the February 2027 implementation date remains feasible.

contrary_evidence: Key enabling rules and standards were still outstanding in 2026, so the product contract could move or change materially.
Battery and digital-product-passport platforms with larger standards teams may already target major manufacturers.
The separate battery due-diligence deadline was postponed, showing that implementation dates can change even when the passport date remains in the current legal text.

economics.acquisition_route: Referrals from BMS integrators and test labs, beginning with one stationary-storage assembler and one downstream installer
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Scenario, not evidence: 80 manufacturers averaging PLN 200,000 annual platform and usage revenue yields PLN 16m revenue; at a 35% operating margin, cumulative distributions over six to eight scaled years could build PLN 20m-plus founder net worth
economics.founder_time: Four hours per day with a strict maximum of two simultaneous integrations until connector reuse is proven
economics.gross_margin_basis: Core hosting, identifier, and schema operations should be high margin, while bespoke BMS connectors and long-term support lower the target blended gross margin to roughly 70%
economics.payback: Target three to six months because integration work must be paid and no custom connector starts without a deposit
economics.pricing: Assumption: PLN 20,000-60,000 per product-line integration plus PLN 15-60 per active battery passport per year with volume discounts
economics.retention_or_repeat: Passports persist across long product lives and new units add usage, producing strong retention if the runtime remains interoperable and durable

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Reusable mappings from battery chemistry, BMS telemetry, component records, and lifecycle status events into permissioned passport fields across recurring pack designs
fingerprint.customer: Polish and Central European assemblers or importers placing industrial batteries above 2 kWh, light-means-of-transport batteries, or specialty EV batteries on the EU market under their own responsibility
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Battery-management-system integrators, testing laboratories, and storage-equipment distributors refer assemblers; a family-installer pilot validates which downstream fields are actually used
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Multi-tenant passport API with QR identifiers, schema versioning, model templates, unit-level BMS and status updates, role-based access, and durable export; integration fee plus per-passport annual usage
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The manufacturer or importer pays an integration fee when the first product line is mapped and pays per active passport when a unique battery identifier is issued or maintained
fingerprint.problem_trigger: From 18 February 2027, covered LMT, industrial batteries above 2 kWh, and EV batteries placed on the market or put into service require an electronic battery passport with model and battery-specific information

founder_fit: Time-series device data, schemas, identity, and anomaly checks use data-engineering strengths
The family renewable installer provides a downstream discovery channel for stationary storage
A single-pack-family integration is a bounded paid pilot compatible with continued employment
Usage revenue can scale across the EU without founder-led content or a camera presence
risks: A standards or deadline change could strand early engineering work.
Long-lived passport availability creates security, continuity, and data-migration obligations.
Incorrect lifecycle or state-of-health data could affect safety and residual-value decisions.
Custom integrations could exceed both the capital cap and the founder's daily time limit.

structure.commercial_archetype: Regulated digital-product-passport infrastructure as a service
structure.control_point: The persistent unique battery identity and access-controlled record from market placement through repurposing or recycling
structure.critical_dependency: Final EU registry, access-right, and service-provider rules plus accurate upstream model and unit data

thesis: A hosted battery-passport runtime can give small and mid-sized industrial-pack and light-mobility assemblers a persistent QR identity, model and serial-level data ingestion, access controls, and lifecycle updates without building passport infrastructure internally. The initial niche is stationary storage packs above 2 kWh, where the founder can observe downstream installer needs through the family renewable business while selling the compliance infrastructure to the upstream economic operator.
title: Battery Passport Runtime for Independent Pack Assemblers
uncertainties: The final interfaces and certification expectations for third-party passport service providers are unresolved.
The number of independent regional pack assemblers and their unit volumes have not been validated.
Customers may prefer a BMS vendor's bundled passport rather than an independent runtime.
The 80-manufacturer wealth scenario assumes cross-border sales and unproven per-unit pricing.
